clue.text: Fresh start in Tulsa bar, AA distraught

indicators.note: someone distraught is all over the place, so the letters before it are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: the letters of the three words, taken together

explanation.surface: A recovering drinker hopes for a new beginning while sitting, upset, in an Oklahoma bar.
explanation.walkthrough: AA (Alcoholics Anonymous) and the bar make a neat scene, but every letter is fodder; 'in' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabula rasa is Latin for a scraped tablet, used idiomatically for a clean slate or new beginning.

clue.text: Grumpy ungulate drinking river

indicators.note: an animal drinking takes something inside itself, so the next word goes within the animal

blocks.note: a moose is a hoofed mammal
R is the standard abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A bad-tempered hoofed animal takes a drink from a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Morose describes a sullen, gloomy, ill-humoured temperament, much the same as grumpy.

clue.text: Guru embraces chief inspector

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold something within one's arms, so the following word sits inside

blocks.note: a guru, a wise prophet, is a seer
arch- as in archenemy means chief

explanation.surface: A spiritual leader hugs a senior police officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chief inspector' reads as a police rank, but the words split: chief is wordplay and inspector alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A searcher is someone who examines or looks closely through things, as an inspector does.

clue.text: In favour of fashion for something positive

blocks.note: pro means for or supporting
ton is an old word for fashion or style

explanation.surface: Someone backs a fashion for upbeat things.
explanation.walkthrough: TON for fashion or style (as in 'bon ton') is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: A proton is a subatomic particle carrying a positive electric charge, so it is literally something positive.

clue.text: Unknown composer, wiping head, consuming hot squash

indicators.note: wiping away the head of a name removes its first letter
consuming means taking something in, so the next letter goes inside

blocks.note: algebra uses x, y and z for unknowns
Giacomo Puccini, Italian opera composer
H for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: An unidentified composer, mopping his brow, eats a hot bowl of squash.
explanation.walkthrough: Puccini loses his P, then H goes inside what remains; Z is put in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Zucchini is the American and Italian name for a courgette, a variety of summer squash.

clue.text: Hand note for pledge

blocks.note: a paw is informally a hand
N is the abbreviation for note

explanation.surface: Handing over a banknote as a pledge or deposit.
explanation.definitionFit: To pawn something is to deposit it as security for a loan, i.e. to pledge it.

clue.text: Sailor with unique seafood specimen

blocks.note: AB, able-bodied seaman
alone in the sense of the only one, unique

explanation.surface: A sailor has a one-of-a-kind specimen of shellfish.
explanation.definitionFit: The abalone is an edible sea snail prized as seafood, so one is an example of a seafood specimen.

clue.text: Arenas in New Hampshire state lacking a bit of spark

indicators.note: lacking means without, so that letter is taken away
making something new means reshaping it, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of both words
a bit of spark is its first letter

explanation.surface: Stadiums in the US state of New Hampshire are short of excitement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Hampshire' looks like the US state name, but 'New' is the anagram signal; one S comes out of the letters before rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: Amphitheatres are open circular venues with tiered seating, the classic arenas of Roman games.

clue.text: In audition, regret critical remark and murmurings

indicators.note: an audition is a hearing, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: to rue is to regret
a barb is a cutting remark

explanation.surface: An actor at an audition regrets a sharp comment and the muttering it caused.
explanation.walkthrough: Actors in crowd scenes say 'rhubarb' repeatedly to make indistinct background chatter, hence the sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhubarb is theatrical slang for the indistinct background chatter of a crowd, so it means murmurings.

clue.text: A Clydebank bee scattered cowpea

indicators.note: things scattered are spread about in disorder, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of all three words

explanation.surface: A bee from Clydebank, the Scottish shipbuilding town, is driven off a pea plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The black-eyed bean is the seed of the cowpea plant, and the two names are used interchangeably.

clue.text: Musk, perhaps, hellish figure Republican included in catalogue

indicators.note: something included in another is placed inside it

blocks.note: Pluto, Roman god of the underworld
cat. is the abbreviation for catalogue
R for Republican

explanation.surface: Elon Musk is listed as a devilish Republican figure.
explanation.walkthrough: Pluto ruled the underworld, hence 'hellish figure'.
explanation.definitionFit: Elon Musk, one of the world's richest men with political influence, is an example of a plutocrat, someone who wields power through wealth.

clue.text: Dance in empty gondola? Steer at the front

indicators.note: emptying a word removes its contents, leaving only the outer letters
this places the steering word before the rest

blocks.note: to con a ship is to steer it
first and last letters of gondola

explanation.surface: A dance in an empty Venetian boat with a steersman up front.
explanation.walkthrough: To con a vessel is the nautical term for directing its steering.
explanation.definitionFit: The conga is a Latin American line dance in which people follow each other in single file.

clue.text: Pointless sit-in an excuse, somewhat

indicators.note: somewhat means to some extent, so only part of the run of words is used

blocks.note: the letters run across sit-in, an and excuse

explanation.surface: Calling a protest sit-in an excuse is rather pointless.
explanation.definitionFit: Inane means silly or lacking sense, and so without any point or purpose.

clue.text: Creation is hard with current employment

blocks.note: H for hard, as on pencils
and means with or together with
I is the symbol for electric current
work is employment

explanation.surface: Making something is tough when you also have a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like an adjective meaning present; in physics I is the symbol for current.
explanation.definitionFit: Handiwork is something made by a particular person, i.e. their creation.

clue.text: About public speaking openings, old man's missing

indicators.note: missing means absent, so those letters are dropped from the word

blocks.note: ora is the Latin plural of os, mouth or opening, used in anatomy
historical means belonging to the past
his is the possessive of he, a man

explanation.surface: A talk on public speaking begins with how the old fellow is absent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old man's' looks like a phrase (old man = father), but old and man's are separate: HIS goes from HISTORICAL. ORA is a Latin plural for openings.
explanation.definitionFit: Oratorical means relating to oratory, the art of formal public speaking.

clue.text: Tougher consuming heart of stout magpie

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle letter
consuming means taking in, so the selected letter goes inside

blocks.note: harder means tougher
middle letter of stout

explanation.surface: A sturdier bird swallowing the centre of a pint of stout.
explanation.walkthrough: Magpies are reputed to collect shiny objects, so the bird name is used for a person who collects compulsively.
explanation.definitionFit: A magpie, figuratively, is a person who obsessively collects and keeps things, which is what a hoarder does.

clue.text: Senior females make money in Japan, part of it remitted

indicators.note: remitted means sent back, so the word is turned round

blocks.note: to do is to make
the yen is Japan's currency
the sen is a hundredth of a yen

explanation.surface: Elder women earn money in Japan and send part of it home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' refers back to the yen: the sen is a subdivision of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A doyenne is the most senior or respected woman in a field, so doyennes are senior females.

clue.text: Can harbours account for secrecy?

indicators.note: to harbour is to shelter something within

blocks.note: can and privy are both slang for a toilet
AC is the abbreviation for account

explanation.surface: Can harbours stay secret about their accounts?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' reads as the verb, but it is the noun meaning toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Privacy is the state of being kept hidden or confidential from others, i.e. secrecy.

clue.text: Dad's attempts to make bakery items

blocks.note: pa is dad, so Dad's is pa's
tries are attempts

explanation.surface: Father has a go at baking.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastries are baked goods made with pastry, sold by bakers, so they are bakery items.

clue.text: Foolish god sent back flower

indicators.note: something sent back is returned the way it came, so read it right to left

blocks.note: silly means foolish
Rama, a Hindu god

explanation.surface: A daft deity returns a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: The amaryllis is a bulb plant grown for its large trumpet-shaped blooms, a kind of flower.

clue.text: Lit LED?

blocks.note: the capitals hint at splitting it after its first letter and joining the two parts with a conjunction

explanation.walkthrough: LED looks like the lighting diode, which suits 'Lit'; but break it into L and ED and it describes L AND ED, giving LANDED.
explanation.definitionFit: Lit is a past tense of alight, to come down onto something, so it means touched down.

clue.text: Idiot protects university storage area

indicators.note: to protect something is to surround and shield it

blocks.note: a clod is a dolt
U for university

explanation.surface: A fool looks after the university's store-room.
explanation.definitionFit: The cloud is online computing space where files are held remotely, a digital place for storage.

clue.text: Secures one hundred lights

blocks.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100
lamps are lights

explanation.surface: Someone fixes up a hundred lamps.
explanation.definitionFit: To clamp is to fasten firmly, so clamps is a verb matching secures.

clue.text: Dance party introduction to nice bird

indicators.note: the introduction to a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: a rave is a dance party
first letter of nice

explanation.surface: At a dance party one is introduced to a pleasant girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird' is British slang for a young woman, which steers the surface away from the feathered sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The raven is a large black bird of the crow family.

clue.text: Electronic vehicle starts rotating device

indicators.note: rotating the start moves the first letter round to the back

blocks.note: E for electronic, as in e-mail
a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: An electric van begins a rotation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rotating device' looks like the definition, but 'rotating' belongs with 'starts' as the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A vane is a blade or plate, such as a weathervane, used as a device to show wind direction or drive a turbine.

clue.text: End of minor informer taken in by unsophisticated story

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter
being taken in by something means going inside it

blocks.note: naive means unsophisticated
last letter of minor
a rat is an informer

explanation.surface: A young informant is fooled by a simple tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrative is an account of connected events, which is a story.

clue.text: Past note is genuine

blocks.note: since means ago, in the past
re is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: An old message turns out to be authentic.
explanation.definitionFit: Sincere means honest and free from pretence, so it is a synonym of genuine.

clue.text: Justify borders of Essex even

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its edges, its outer letters

blocks.note: first and last letters of Essex
even ground is plain, flat land

explanation.surface: Defend the flatness of Essex's boundaries.
explanation.walkthrough: Essex is an English county known for being low and flat.
explanation.definitionFit: To explain one's actions is to give reasons for them, which is to justify them.
